title: The scaffold ships node-pg-migrate and the generated app migrates green
description:
SPIDR child 1 of task-8f86e10504c74e248ccfa6f427b41a15 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). Dependency-free LEAF.

ARCHITECT DECISION on the question the parent left open ("architect picks drizzle-kit or node-pg-migrate; pinned"): NODE-PG-MIGRATE. Reasons, so it is not re-litigated: (1) drizzle-kit implies adopting DRIZZLE ORM as the generated product's data layer - a far larger commitment that constrains how every future node writes schema and query code, for a row whose subject is only migrations; (2) this feature needs first-class REVERT (`db:migrate:down`, and `deployment.migrate_down` reverting the last batch), and node-pg-migrate has an explicit up/down per migration while SQL-diff generators handle down poorly; (3) plain migration files are easier for a CODING SEAT to author correctly than a schema file plus generated diffs, and seats are who will write them; (4) it is PostgreSQL-specific, which matches the controlled profile exactly. PIN THE VERSION.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the scaffold profile's migration surface - the pinned tool, `pnpm db:migrate` and `pnpm db:migrate:down` scripts, a `migrations/` directory with an initial migration - and the proof that the generated app actually migrates against a real disposable PostgreSQL. No verifier leg, no deploy, no UI.

COORDINATION, NOT A DEPENDENCY: the scaffold generator belongs to task-4a0f706437a042059789be2ebdb98bc0 (under the repository-bootstrapping parent), whose golden test pins the generated tree under a PROFILE VERSION constant. This row CHANGES that tree, so it is a profile version BUMP, not an edit in place, and that row's golden test moves with it. Check which of the two landed first and coordinate - do not fork a second scaffold.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): no migration tooling anywhere. `grep -rn 'db:migrate|MIGRATION_' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` finds only unrelated scheduler fairness constants (fairness-cap-revision.ts:53, fairness-aging.ts:110). The gap is real.

THE LOCKFILE IS THIS ROW'S REAL HAZARD AND THE DoD DOES NOT MENTION IT. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 5 files, 1 new.

Tool decision left as-is — rail 1 settles it and the four reasons hold, particularly first-class per-migration down, which is what `deployment.migrate_down` needs later.

## The lockfile

The scaffold emits a **committed** `pnpm-lock.yaml` (generator.ts:129), and both the generated README (root-templates.ts:114) and its CI workflow (:169) run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. That file's own header states the rule: *"VERSION PINS are what make `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` hold in the generated product… Editing any of them is a profile VERSION BUMP plus a lockfile re-mint, not an edit in place."*

So a package.json gaining node-pg-migrate whose lockfile did not is a **frozen-lockfile failure in every product this profile ever generates** — while moe-next's own gates stay green throughout. Drill (i) reverts the lockfile bytes and requires the child install to fail.

## The bump retires `controlled-1` by construction

`isKnownProfileVersion` (generator.ts:74) is `value === CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION` — a strict single-value equality. Bump to `controlled-2` and every `controlled-1` request refuses `BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN`.

I measured what that strands: `CONTROLLED_PROFILE_VERSION`/`profileVersion` appear **nowhere** outside `controlled-profile/`, nothing persists a version, and the bootstrap command that would write one (task-facff1d1) is still PLANNING. So retiring strands nothing *today* — but it is a decision to state, not to stumble into, and the plan makes the worker re-run that grep in case the bootstrap row landed meanwhile.

## DoD-5 is easier than it reads — don't over-build it

node-pg-migrate timestamps filenames when **its CLI** creates one. The scaffold **writes the initial migration itself** as a template, so its name is hardcoded and determinism is free. The real question is what a coding seat does authoring migration two — and the golden test only pins the scaffold's tree, so accepting timestamps there is defensible. The plan asks for that decision rather than a ritual defence against a problem the generator does not have.

## The expensive proof already has a precedent that solves its hardest problem

`controlled-profile-build.test.ts` gates its build arm behind `MOE_SCAFFOLD_BUILD=1` because unconditionally it *"would execute inside `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, the gate every row on this board runs, and would red on any offline host — making every later gate on the board inadmissible."* A migration arm needs a live database and is strictly worse on that axis.

Its header also documents the two things that stop an opt-in becoming a decoration, both carried into step 4: an **always-on** arm asserting the preconditions whose absence would make the expensive arm vacuous, and a completion record quoting the expensive arm's own output with a **zero skipped** count.

## One tripwire in the golden test

`differing == ["README.md", "package.json"]` (generator.test.ts:170-182) asserts the product name reaches exactly two files. If the migration or its config embeds the product name, that arm reds — and the fix is to keep the name **out of the migration files**, not to widen the expected list.

Two contracts children 2 and 3 will build on, so state both: whether `db:migrate:down` reverts **one** migration or **all**, and where `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` is exercised given it is defined here and raised there.
